title: Deep learning predicts H. pylori antibiotic resistance from routine H&E gastric biopsies
summary: A weakly supervised framework predicted PCR-confirmed Helicobacter pylori resistance from gastric biopsy whole-slide images in a multicenter cohort of 755 patients. In the independent test set (n = 151) the AUC was 0.903 for clarithromycin and 0.959 for fluoroquinolone resistance, with sensitivity of 85.2% and 98.1% at the default threshold. Vision-language models (Qwen3-VL, MedGemma) filtered patches before VIRCHOW2 encoding and cross-attention aggregation. The test set came from the same multicenter cohort and the abstract itself calls for prospective validation.
ai_technology: VLM patch filtering (Qwen3-VL, MedGemma), VIRCHOW2 foundation-model encoder and cross-attention aggregation predicting clarithromycin and fluoroquinolone resistance
organization: The Eighth Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University

evidence.tested: Independent test set (n = 151) within a multicenter cohort of 755 patients, with PCR-confirmed resistance phenotypes as ground truth.
evidence.unknown: Performance on a separate prospective cohort; the abstract states prospective validation is pending.
evidence.ai_role: Zero-shot vision-language patch filtering, a pathology foundation-model encoder and attention-based slide-level aggregation predicted resistance phenotypes from H&E slides.
